_comment: What a cloud routine session's GitHub egress actually permits, probed on
2026-08-11 by `scripts/probe_github_access.py --pr 235 --writes` running inside
a routine (trigger `probe: gh-proxy`, since disabled). Repository and SHA are
real; nothing is edited.
Its job is the same as cowork_webhook_live.json's: pin a fact about an outside
system that nothing in this repo would otherwise record, and that several
design decisions rest on. Re-derive it by re-running the probe, never by
editing this file by feel.
THE STORY THIS REPLACES. `cron/cd-deploy.md` was a no-op on every firing for
weeks. The diagnosis on record was 'the session has no `gh`' — true, and
incomplete in the way that matters: a run on 2026-08-11 installed `gh`,
confirmed GH_TOKEN was set, and still got 403. The binary was never the
constraint. Outbound GitHub goes through a proxy with its own allowlist.
FOUR THINGS FOLLOW, and each one closes off an approach that looks obvious:
1. Installing `gh` cannot fix the routine prose. `gh pr list --json` and
`gh issue list --json` are GraphQL underneath, and GraphQL is refused
outright — so the `--json` reads the sweeps and the digest are built on
are exactly what a bootstrapped `gh` would still fail at.
2. The variables half of cd-deploy's `--strict` step can never work in-session,
any transport. `/actions/variables` is refused on read AND write, so it
moved to .github/workflows/cowork-repo-setup.yml, where a runner has no
such proxy.
3. The labels half genuinely IS fixed by the REST transport: `gh label list`
is GraphQL and was refused, while `GET /repos/{slug}/labels` is permitted.
4. `pr_feedback.py` cannot answer fully in a routine session at all, and must
not pretend to: `reviewDecision` and thread resolution exist only in v4,
and POSTing the commit status is refused too. Its full path belongs to
.github/workflows/pr-feedback.yml, where `gh` and a real token both work.
NOTE the refusal message names the sanctioned alternative itself: 'Use REST
via `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/...` instead'. REST is the supported path;
GraphQL is not available and is not going to be.
One asymmetry worth keeping in view: `/actions/runs` is permitted while
`/actions/variables` is not, so the block is repo-admin scoped, not a blanket
ban on `/actions/`.
